- If sentiment is positive (≥ 0.2) and forecast is trending upward, reduce forecast slope to avoid over-optimism.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤ -0.2) and forecast is trending downward, increase forecast slope to avoid underreaction.  
- After a sharp price spike, model tends to overcorrect — reduce forecast magnitude in next 3–5 periods.  
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days of decline after peak), model often fails to recognize — adjust forecast to reflect gradual decline.  
- For 30-day horizon, if history shows volatility or sentiment shifts, model often underestimates volatility — increase forecast spread or add buffer.  
- If sentiment history has multiple small positive spikes, model tends to ignore them — adjust forecast to reflect cumulative sentiment bias.  
- If forecast is flat or slowly rising while true outcome shows strong upward momentum, model is lagging — increase forecast slope by 10–20% for next 3–5 periods.
